change_note: Technical checklist (technical_checklist): the eight steps from the household's video, computed daily from end-of-day bars and measured.

routines.name: Pre-market brief
routines.why: Information arrives overnight. Gaps, filings and headlines on watchlist names set the day's context before prices react. Code only: it lists events and does not interpret them.

routines.name: Fetch daily prices
routines.why: End-of-day bars for the watchlist and benchmark, fetched after the close. Raw bars stay inside the run (provider licence); only derived returns, distances and indexed lines are published. One failed symbol fails the run.

routines.name: Daily brain run
routines.why: The core loop, run by itself each market morning as a scheduled Claude Code session on the household's Claude subscription: build the pack, run the brain, then brain.yml re-checks and records it or writes nothing. A second firing catches a late data run; a day already recorded is skipped.

routines.name: Score matured picks
routines.why: Without scoring there is no feedback. Each pick is compared with the benchmark after the horizon, so the measure is excess return, not luck from a rising market.

routines.name: Regime and risk monitor
routines.why: The same signal behaves differently in calm and stressed markets. Benchmark volatility, drawdown and trend set a regime tag that the packer passes to the brain.

routines.name: Goal check and portfolio rule
routines.why: The household goal is a diversified 4-5 stock satellite and +20% a year. This tests the rule over ~9 years against holding every name, the S&P 500 core and the benchmark, and counts how often +20% actually happened.

routines.name: Paper portfolio (forward only)
routines.why: Backtests can be re-fitted; a forward record cannot. Holdings are written once a month with that day's data and never edited, so the track is an honest test before any money moves.

routines.name: Rule backtests
routines.why: Tests each pre-registered rule (savings cadence, satellite selection) on the full history against random baskets from the same names, with costs and a next-close fill. Evidence only: history never moves money; the forward paper record does.

routines.name: Forward ledger of every rule
routines.why: History can be re-fitted; a forward record cannot. On the first run of each month every testable rule's holdings are written down with only that day's data and never edited. Months later this is the evidence that decides which rules deserve money.

routines.name: Score people's public calls
routines.why: Learn from them, but measure them. Each dated public call of a person we follow is scored against the S&P 500 core from the first trading day after it became public, over 13, 26 and 52 weeks. Fewer than ten half-year-old calls proves nothing.

routines.name: Technical checklist
routines.why: The household's eight-step video checklist (candle, trend, volume, twenty-day average, gaps, levels, RSI, risk plan) for every name after each close, what flipped since yesterday, and how it did in history and forward. Unproven for us: measured, never trusted.

routines.name: News and social digest
routines.why: Attention moves prices in the short run. It counts mentions and links per watchlist name from followed sources and stores derived signals only, never post text.

routines.name: Opportunity scan
routines.why: The watchlist goes stale. A code screen looks beyond it for relative-strength leaders, unusual volume and new highs, then one call writes a short case for each candidate. You merge or reject the PR.

routines.name: Thesis and invalidation review
routines.why: Every pick states what would prove it wrong. This checks open picks against their own invalidation conditions, which guards against sunk-cost thinking.

routines.name: Sector rotation and breadth
routines.why: Index moves hide what is underneath. Sector relative strength and breadth show whether leadership is broad, which is healthy, or narrow, which is fragile.

routines.name: Earnings and macro calendar
routines.why: Scheduled events such as earnings, rate decisions and inflation prints create jump risk. The brain should know when a pick's horizon spans one.

routines.name: Cost and hygiene audit
routines.why: The system's own costs compound too. It tracks cost per run, pack growth and lint warnings, and opens an issue before the budget drifts.

routines.name: Factor and style check
routines.why: Returns are partly explained by common factors such as momentum, value, quality and size. Knowing which style is being paid tells you whether a pick is skill or factor exposure.

routines.name: Conviction calibration
routines.why: A forecaster is useful only if confidence matches outcomes. It checks whether high-conviction picks really beat low ones, by stance, and whether conviction carries any information.

routines.name: Monthly post-mortem
routines.why: Turns scored outcomes into candidate lessons with evidence. The model drafts and a person decides, so the brain never edits its own rules.

routines.name: Library ingest
routines.why: Books and lectures become short, paraphrased, tagged principles with a citation. No source text is committed, and you approve each batch.
